title: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall
text:
According to the Book of Nehemiah, Nehemiah was cupbearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes when he heard that the walls of Jerusalem still lay in ruins and its gates were burned. He asked the king's permission to go and rebuild them, and the king sent him with letters and supplies.

In Jerusalem, Nehemiah first rode out quietly at night to inspect the broken walls. Then he gathered the people and divided the work. Chapter 3 of the book lists who built what: the high priest and his fellow priests rebuilt the Sheep Gate, the men of Jericho built the next stretch, a goldsmith and a perfumer each repaired a section, a man and his daughters built another. Many families repaired the part of the wall directly in front of their own houses. The text even notes that the nobles of one town would not bend their necks to the work.

Local enemies mocked them, saying that even a fox would knock their stone wall down, and then they threatened to attack. Nehemiah set guards and organized the people so that half worked and half stood ready with spears, while every builder kept a sword at his side. A trumpeter stayed with him to call everyone together if an attack came.

The book says the wall was finished in fifty-two days.
lesson: Large projects move fast when each group owns a clear piece, especially one close to home. Keep both building and guarding in view when people want the work to fail.
people: Nehemiah, the people of Jerusalem, Sanballat, Tobiah
source: Book of Nehemiah, chapters 2 to 4 and 6:15
